$comment: Measured facts for EBV EBNA1 disruption. Unlike direct excision, this exploits a biological dependency: EBV episomes require EBNA1 for replication. Disrupt the gene and cell division does the rest.

subject.mechanism: CRISPR disruption of EBNA1 → episome replication failure → dilution over cell divisions
subject.therapeutic_effect: EBV episome lost from dividing cells within 2-3 weeks
subject.selectivity: Only EBV+ cells contain EBNA1 target sequence
subject.model: EBV+ cell lines (C666-1, NPC43) and primary NPC cultures
subject.key_insight: You don't excise the virus — you break its replication machinery and let mitosis finish the job

data.note: 65% indel in EBNA1 is the therapeutic outcome — frameshifts abolish EBNA1 function. The episome then fails to replicate. After 14 days, >95% of EBNA1-disrupted cells show complete EBV genome loss.
